Before the battle the priests of Ulric have lit a great fire, a spark of the Eternal Flame carried from Middenheim. The warriors gather around it in silence. The Wolf takes no lives, the priests say, but he wants to see what we are willing to give up for victory.
I give the gods my own blood: [scoped_war_sacrifice.GetTitledFirstName].
I give the Dark Prince the dearest thing I have: [scoped_war_sacrifice.GetTitledFirstName].
Kin-blood for the Horned Rat! Take [scoped_war_sacrifice.GetFirstName]!
Take [sacrificed_courtier.GetFirstName]. The gods will not miss a servant.
Give [sacrificed_courtier.GetFirstName] to the Dark Prince. Slowly.
Feed-give [sacrificed_courtier.GetFirstName] to the altar. Slave-meat is still meat.
[sacrificed_commander_khorne.GetFirstName]! Fight me before the altar. One skull for the Throne!
I give [scoped_war_sacrifice.GetTitledFirstName], and let the Changer of Ways decide what it is worth.
[scoped_war_sacrifice.GetFirstName] shall drink from the cauldron and share in the Grandfather's gifts.
I will drink from the cauldron myself.
Let one of my provinces feel the Grandfather's love.
Throw the best of the plunder on the pyre.
Skulls, cattle and gold, on the altar! Blood is blood.
Burn the finest of the spoils, silks and wine and all.
Give the Horned Rat the warpstone and the shiny-things. Some of them. Fine, all of them.
I will swear a blood oath at the flame, and cut my own hand to seal it.
Throw the spoils of our last battle into the fire. We fight for the Wolf, not for gold.
Not now. The battle can wait for its offering.
You will fight §Y[sacrificed_commander_khorne.GetTitledFirstName]§! to the death. The Blood God will take one skull or the other.
The Changer of Ways decides how much favour the offering wins: it may be great, or it may be small and last longer.

The offering is made. A great roar goes up from the warband, and for a moment the smoke above the pyre seems to twist into shapes that watch us. The warriors take it for a sign. They will fight like daemons in the battle to come.

It is done, and the altar is red. The warband bellows the Blood God's name until their throats are raw, and the earth seems to drink what was spilled. Khorne has seen. My warriors will fight like nothing can kill them.

It is done. The flies rise from the cauldron in a great buzzing cloud and settle on the warband like a blessing. The warriors laugh and scratch at their new sores. Grandfather Nurgle is pleased, and in the battle to come my enemies will learn how generous he can be.

It is done. For a heartbeat the fire in the circle burns every colour at once, and every warrior in the camp hears a different voice laughing. No one can say what the Changer of Ways has promised, but the warband marches with a strange certainty that the battle is already won.

It is done. A sweet, heavy perfume rolls out over the camp, and the warriors shiver with something that is not quite pain and not quite pleasure. The Dark Prince has tasted the offering. My warriors will throw themselves into the battle as if it were a lover.

It is done-done! The grey seers twitch and chitter and swear they saw the Horned Rat's shadow on the cave wall. The clanrats are squeaking with excitement. For once they might even fight instead of running. For a while.

It is done. The flame leaps up white and blue, and in the howling of the wind the warriors hear the voice of the Wolf. They raise their axes and hammers and roar Ulric's name into the night. No one in this host will take a step back in the battle to come.
The gods are with us!
Victory-victory is ours! Probably.
Ulric! Ulric! Ulric!

The great monoliths of Norsca mark the cairns of fallen champions, and the Gods watch over them. Your deeds are worth a stone of their own. Raise a monolith, have the runes cut deep, and let those who come after you read what you did.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName].

A warrior who only fights soon forgets why. Open your hall, fill the horns, sit in the sweat-lodge with the others and boast until the roof shakes. The warriors must know your face over a cup as well as over a shield.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName].

Between the raids the clans must eat, and the beasts of the north grow bolder every winter. Take your spears into the forests and the ice. Bring back meat for the clan, or better, the carcass of something tainted and huge for the skalds to sing about.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName].

The time has come again to feast the ancestors in your hall. Let the skald recount their sagas, pour their share of the mead, and remind them whose blood still carries their name. The dead fight beside those who remember them.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. You have given yourself to war, and the tribes have noticed. Battle and the Gods are the heart of the north, and you have put both first.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. The jarls are pleased to hear of your Great Blot. The Vitki says the Gods have tasted the blood and will remember who poured it.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. Your monolith stands. Those with the courage to look closely will read your saga in the runes long after the crows have had you.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. They tell me you drank three warriors under the benches and challenged a fourth to wrestle a bear. Norscans are braggarts, but now they brag about you.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. The clan has meat, and the skalds have a new verse about you and the beast you brought down. Chaos spawn, ice drake or sea-serpent, it grows larger with every telling.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. The ancestors have been fed and remembered. May they stand beside your sworn warriors when the shield wall breaks.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
For glory!
The skalds make a §Ysaga§! of your deeds.

The warrior [From.GetBestName] has come to my hall and sworn the blood-oath on my axe. [From.GetFirstName] is a fearsome [From.GetManWoman], scarred and hungry, and soon we will share in the bloodshed to come.
Skol, [From.GetFirstName]!

The warriors of my hall can lift more, run further and swing harder than I can, and every one of them knows it. A shieldmaiden who cannot keep up with the shield wall is only a woman with a shield. Something has to change.
I will pull an oar on the longship every dawn.
I will run the hills with my hound.
A new mail shirt. Look the part and the rest follows.
I am strong enough as I am.
Nothing changes.
Weeks after I lost my hound on the hills it came limping into the yard, thin, filthy and wagging, with half a wolf's ear in its teeth.
A herdsman came down from the hills with a collar he found among the rocks. Whatever took my hound out there, it did not leave much else.
Good dog. Who is a good dog?
The hills take what they want.

The shield wall has buckled and [my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] is fighting alone, cut off from the warriors, with three of the enemy closing in. I am close enough to do something about it. I am also close enough to do nothing, and no one would ever know.
Throw my shield in front of [my_liege.GetHerHim]!
You hurl your shield at the nearest attacker.
[my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] lives.
[my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] is hurt.
Throw my spear!
You throw your spear at the leader of the attackers. A great cast, or a terrible one.
Everyone will see the cast.
Everyone will see the miss.
Let the Gods decide.
You keep your shield and your spear to yourself.
[my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] dies.
[my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] fights free on [my_liege.GetHerHis] own.
My shield caught the first attacker full in the face and the others hesitated. That was enough. [my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] is alive.
My shield went wide. One of the attackers got his blade into [my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] before the warriors closed in around us.
My spear took their leader through the throat and pinned him to the mud. The rest broke and ran. Half the shield wall saw it, and they will not stop talking about it.
I missed. Worse, I stepped forward to throw and put myself between the attackers and [my_liege.GetTitledFirstName]. They were glad of the easier target.
[my_liege.GetFirstName] lives.
That should have been mine to stop.
[my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] is maimed, and you are blamed.
Let the skalds sing that one.
[my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] will remember this.
I will carry this wound for the rest of my life.
You are maimed, and the warriors laugh at the throw.
I was alone and surrounded when a shield came spinning out of nowhere and laid out the nearest of them. [From.GetFirstName] was right behind it. Without [From.GetHerHim] I would be feeding the crows.

I was alone and surrounded when [From.GetFirstName]'s spear went through their leader's throat. The others ran. The whole shield wall saw it, and they cheered [From.GetHerHim] louder than they have ever cheered me.
I owe you my life.
Your shieldmaiden saved your life.
There is no better shield in the north.
I watched them cut [my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] down. It did not take long. No one saw me hold back, and no one will ever ask.
I held back and waited for the end, but [my_liege.GetTitledFirstName] fought free alone, bloodied and furious. Now [my_liege.GetSheHe] is asking where [my_liege.GetHerHis] shieldmaiden was.
The Gods decided.
I was cut off. That is my story.
I am alone, the warriors are too far away, and the last blade is already coming down. My shieldmaiden [From.GetFirstName] is right there, watching.
I fought free of them alone. When it was over I found my shieldmaiden [From.GetFirstName] a few paces off, unblooded. [From.GetSheHe] says [From.GetSheHe] was cut off.
A shieldmaiden who cannot reach me is no shieldmaiden.
[From.GetFirstName] tried to shield me and missed. The blade that got past [From.GetHerHim] got into me.
[From.GetFirstName] tried to throw a spear for me, missed, and took the blades meant for me. [From.GetSheHe] will live, but not whole.
I will live with it.
You are maimed.
[From.GetSheHe] paid for it.
Your shieldmaiden is maimed.

The enemy broke through on the left and my shieldmaiden [my_shieldmaiden.GetFirstName] threw [my_shieldmaiden.GetHerHis] shield into the gap. I saw [my_shieldmaiden.GetHerHim] go down under three of them before the warriors dragged [my_shieldmaiden.GetHerHim] clear.
Get [my_shieldmaiden.GetHerHim] to the healers!
Your shieldmaiden is badly hurt.
I held the gap and it cost me. I remember the axe and then the mud, and then nothing.
The gap held.
You are maimed.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut, staring at the roof. The wounds are healing badly. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut, turning [From.GetHerHis] head to see the door with the eye [From.GetSheHe] has left. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut, glaring at the crutch by the bed. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut, trying to buckle a shield strap with one hand. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut, with [From.GetHerHis] back to the door so no one would see [From.GetHerHis] face. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut. The healers say it is a wonder [From.GetSheHe] lives at all. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
I found [From.GetFirstName] alone in the healing hut, staring at the roof. [From.GetSheHe] has not said a word to anyone in days.
My own healer will see to you.
Your healer tends to your shieldmaiden.
You are not alone in this hall.
You sit with your shieldmaiden a while.
You held the gap. No one else could have.
You praise your shieldmaiden in front of the warriors.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] sent [From.GetHerHis] own healer, a sour old woman with cold hands and foul ointments. It hurts worse than the axe did, but the wounds are closing at last.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] came and sat by my bed and talked of nothing much, of the ships and the weather and the sagas, for most of the evening. I did not know how much I needed that.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] stood in the hall and told the warriors that I held the gap when no one else could have. They beat their shields for me. I could hear it from the healing hut.
I will be back on my feet soon.

[From.GetFirstName] is on [From.GetHerHis] feet again, and we were walking along the boat sheds when something small and furious shot out from under a hull. A half-wild kitten, all claws and spite, now clinging to [From.GetFirstName]'s boot.

[From.GetFirstName] and I have taken to walking along the boat sheds in the evenings. Tonight something small and furious shot out from under a hull and attacked [From.GetHerHis] boot: a half-wild kitten, all claws and spite.
[From.GetFirstName] was showing me the new shield-boss the smith made when something small and furious shot out from under a hull and attacked it: a half-wild kitten, all claws and spite.
It has the heart of a warrior. It is mine.
You keep the kitten.
It chose you. Keep it.
Your shieldmaiden keeps the kitten.
My little one will love it.
One of your children gets the kitten.
Leave it. It belongs to the sheds.
The kitten goes back under its hull.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has the kitten now. It bites everyone who comes near except [From.GetHerHim]. I suppose they deserve each other.
The kitten sleeps on my mail shirt and hisses at the warriors. [From.GetTitledFirstName] laughs every time [From.GetSheHe] sees it.
We left the kitten to its hull. It still comes out to spit at us whenever [From.GetTitledFirstName] and I walk past.
A fitting pair.
My little warrior.
Some things are better wild.

[shieldmaiden_liege.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me to take up the shield and stand at [shieldmaiden_liege.GetHerHis] side as a shieldmaiden: to fight in the front rank, to guard [shieldmaiden_liege.GetHerHim] in battle and to answer to no one else.
I will be your shield.
Find someone else.
You will not be asked again for a year.
[From.GetFirstName] has taken up the shield. The smith wants paying for the mail, but every warrior in the hall saw [From.GetHerHim] swear.
A good day for my hall.
[From.GetFirstName] will not take up the shield.
So be it.
[shieldmaiden_liege.GetTitledFirstName] has taken my shield from me. Apparently a shieldmaiden who falls out of the longship is not what the hall needs.
[shieldmaiden_liege.GetTitledFirstName] has released me from the shield with thanks and gifts. I served well, and everyone knows it.
[shieldmaiden_liege.GetTitledFirstName] has taken my shield from me. [shieldmaiden_liege.GetSheHe] has not forgotten the day I let the enemy through.
[shieldmaiden_liege.GetTitledFirstName] has released me from the shield. My wounds have done what the enemy could not.
[shieldmaiden_liege.GetTitledFirstName] has released me from the shield. My days in the front rank are over.
I understand.
You are no longer a shieldmaiden.
Go a-Viking
$WHO$ has been asked by the Jarl of $SOCIETY$ to take the longships out and come home with a story.
Go a-Viking and come home.
The Jarl has sent word: the longships are idle and the young men grow fat. Take them out, go a-viking, and come home with plunder and a story for the hall.

Skol, [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName]. You took the longships out and brought them home again, heavy with plunder. The skalds are already arguing over the verses.\n\n[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
The longships are ready.
Not this summer.
